title: Least Loss of Passive Phase Shifters
description: LaTeX source, numerical checks (421) and a Lean 4 certificate (87 theorems) of the finite and algebraic parts of the paper Least Loss of Passive Phase Shifters. The paper proves that a passive causal system without zeros in the upper half-plane cannot shift every frequency of a band [a,b] by the same phase theta > 0 without loss: its mean attenuation over the band is at least theta (K(kappa) - E(kappa))/kappa nepers, kappa = (b-a)/(b+a), and an explicit system has the least attenuation at every frequency of the band at once. With zeros allowed, one explicit system with a single zero has the least attenuation at every frequency at once; for a right angle its mean attenuation is (pi/2)(sqrt b - sqrt a)/(sqrt b + sqrt a) nepers. With a delay added to the phase, the least mean loss without zeros is found in closed form and stays above a positive floor; with zeros the optimal system exists and is unique, with a test for optimality, and its loss falls exponentially with the delay, at a rate between a/e and pi ab/(b-a).
